findings.title: Login IDP cache is not invalidated when updating an IDP linked to a disabled organization
findings.body: In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, `idpById` is fetched via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which wraps the model using `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to return `false` whenever the linked organization (or `OrganizationProvider`) is disabled; `model` is likewise wrapped if the caller obtained it from `session.identityProviders()`. However, the login cache in `getForLogin` is populated from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` (which only checks the IDP's own `enabled` state in the database), and enabling or disabling an organization does not invalidate `cacheKeyForLogin`. As a result, if an organization is disabled while one of its login IDPs is updated to no longer qualify for login (e.g., setting `hideOnLogin` to `true`, `linkOnly` to `true`, or `BROKER_PUBLIC` to `false`)—or if a wrapped model is updated to become login-eligible—`getLoginPredicate().test(original)` and `getLoginPredicate().test(updated)` both return `false` because `isEnabled()` returns `false` on the wrapper. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` then returns early without invalidating the login caches. When the organization is re-enabled, `getForLogin` will continue serving the stale login IDP set (and since `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` only re-checks `idp.isEnabled()`, hidden, link-only, or non-public IDPs will still be shown on the login page).

findings.title: Test cleanup references literal "alias" instead of the created IDP alias, leaking realm IDPs
findings.body: In `testCacheIDPForLogin` (lines 381 and 425), cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` using the literal string `"alias"` instead of `idpRep.getAlias()`. Because no IDP named `"alias"` exists, each cleanup call throws `NotFoundException` (which `TestCleanup` ignores), and the realm-level IDPs created by the test (`idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-9`, which are not deleted when the test organizations are removed) are leaked into the test realm for subsequent tests.
